items.title: [apnews.com] European-Japanese BepiColombo enters Mercury orbit ahead of two-probe science mission
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

BepiColombo, a joint mission of the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, entered orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21, completing an eight-year journey and becoming the second mission to orbit the planet. The two orbiters remain attached; they are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10 and take up different polar orbits, with science operations due to begin in April 2027. The mission will use the European Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Japan’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio, to study Mercury from separate vantage points. Their instruments are designed to examine the planet’s surface and interior, its magnetic field and the thin gas envelope around it, including how the magnetic field interacts with the solar wind. Controllers in Germany confirmed the spacecraft’s capture several hours after a series of braking thruster firings, with the spacecraft about 152 million kilometers away. A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival from December 2025. Its nominal science mission is planned to last one Earth year, with an extension through 2029.

items.title: [bbc.com] Brazil activates protective measures after about 20 isolated Awá approach
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

About 20 Indigenous Awá living in isolation approached the Guajajara village of Tawari on Monday, November 16, in Arariboia Indigenous Territory, in the Brazilian state of Maranhão; they received yams and returned to the forest. Members of the Guajajara community recorded the encounter, and the organization Survival International shared the footage. The National Foundation for Indigenous Peoples (Funai) and Indigenous health personnel are in the area. The government activated an emergency coordination mechanism to assess the situation and health risks. Authorities said they are still assessing the initial information and that this isolated approach does not mean the Awá have abandoned their isolation. The reason for the visit has not been confirmed; Survival International linked it to pressure from illegal loggers, hunters, and ranchers on the territory. Local residents voiced concern about the thinness of some children and older people. There is also concern about the risk of infections, given the group’s limited exposure to common pathogens.

items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

The European-Japanese BepiColombo mission is due to enter orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21 after an eight-year journey of about 6 billion miles, becoming only the second mission to orbit the planet. Its two orbiters will investigate Mercury’s surface, interior and magnetic environment, including its unusually large metal core, the origins of its magnetic field and ice in permanently shadowed craters. A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival, and reaching Mercury requires careful braking against the Sun’s gravity. The European Mercury Planetary Orbiter will map the surface’s composition and study the interior; Japan’s orbiter will measure the magnetic field and the planet’s thin sodium exosphere. The spacecraft are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10, with science operations planned to begin in April 2027.

items.title: [winnipegfreepress.com] Federal memo warns freshwater pressures threaten Canada’s long-term security
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

An internal federal memo warns that growing pressure on freshwater supplies could harm Canada’s long-term security and prosperity. It says it is unclear whether the country can meet future needs as its cities and economy grow. The Canada Water Agency prepared the document for Environment Minister Julie Dabrusin as work proceeds on a national water security strategy. Dabrusin called the strategy a “mission critical priority” in response to Prime Minister Mark Carney’s request for cabinet priorities. The memo links water risks to climate change, pollution, population growth, overuse and aging infrastructure. Public consultation ran from Sept. 9 to Oct. 25, and the agency also consulted provincial, territorial and Indigenous partners. The memo calls for an assessment of water protection and sustainable management, including shared waters with the United States and global water risks. The 12-page memo was obtained through an access-to-information request, with some material withheld.

items.title: [healio.com] Children with atopic dermatitis show higher odds of sleep disturbance
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Children and young adults with atopic dermatitis had 28% higher odds of sleep disturbance than peers without the condition, a retrospective review of 26,395 patients at an urban primary care clinic found. The association remained after researchers accounted for coexisting atopy and mental health conditions; neither significantly changed the link. The study included patients aged 0 to 21; 14.5% had atopic dermatitis and 10.3% had sleep disturbance. Samantha Sundermeier, DO, an attending physician at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, said future studies should assess disease severity, treatment response and sleep over time using validated measures and patient-reported outcomes.

items.title: [ft.com] COP31 draft drops fossil-fuel exit as carbon-capture target advances
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

A revised draft for the COP31 United Nations climate summit gives carbon capture a prominent role, proposing a target—still under debate—to capture at least 500 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year by 2035, with a longer-term range of 1.3 billion to 2.5 billion tonnes. Climate experts warn the costly technology has not been proven at the scale required and could be used to justify continued fossil-fuel production. Australia and Turkey issued the nine-page draft in Antalya on Nov. 19. It removes all references to coal, oil and gas and to transitioning away from fossil fuels. It retains a proposed goal to increase electricity’s share of global final energy demand to 35% by 2035, but does not specify that the power must come from clean sources. The revision also removed a proposed $120 billion annual adaptation-finance target for developing countries by 2035 and deferred further decisions on tripling adaptation finance to COP32. Separately, the Pacific Resilience Facility remained about $300 million short of its $500 million goal, according to reporting from Antalya.

items.title: [ft.com] Investors at COP31 warn of rising systemic financial risk
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Forty large pension funds, insurers and sovereign wealth funds warned at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya that climate impacts threaten financial stability. Investors at a closed-door meeting said climate finance needs private capital, but some asset owners remain cautious about emerging-market projects because they lack reliable ways to assess and manage the risks. Developing countries including India are pressing for clearer obligations and more adaptation funding, while the European Union favors using existing finance mechanisms rather than creating a new work program. Outside the talks, organizers said more than 10,000 people joined a Nov. 14 climate march calling for grants, support for affected communities and a transition away from fossil fuels. Negotiators have a 104-paragraph climate-finance draft, released Nov. 14, and are due to continue discussions on finance and a just transition in the summit’s second week.

items.title: [nation.com.pk] WHO warns rising drug resistance is eroding last-line antibiotic options
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Drug-resistant bacterial infections are increasing across regions. The World Health Organization and European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control report that European Klebsiella pneumoniae infections rose 72% from 2019 to 2025, while resistance in monitored E. coli infections also increased. Globally, one in six laboratory-confirmed common bacterial infections was resistant to antibiotics in 2023, according to the WHO. When standard antibiotics fail, clinicians may turn to carbapenems, but resistance to these last-line drugs is also rising. In the Americas, carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae increased from about 15% in 2015 to 26% in 2024; median resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii was 77% across the seven reporting countries. Health authorities are calling for stronger infection prevention, laboratory diagnosis and surveillance; the Pan American Health Organization’s 2027–2031 action plan was approved in September.

items.title: [pewresearch.org] Pew projects Muslims will surpass Christians globally by 2035
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Muslims are projected to become the world’s largest religious group by 2035, reaching 2.57 billion people compared with 2.52 billion Christians, according to new projections from the Pew Research Center. Both populations are expected to grow, but the Muslim population is projected to increase faster, mainly because Muslim women had an average of 3.1 children in 2020-2025, compared with 2.5 among Christian women. Pew estimates there were 2.02 billion Muslims and 2.27 billion Christians in 2020. If current trends continue, the Muslim population will exceed 3.6 billion by 2070, while the Christian population will remain just below 3 billion. The world population is projected to grow 29% over the same period. The report models demographic patterns across 201 countries and territories, including age, fertility, mortality, migration and religious switching. Its projections do not account for events such as wars, epidemics or natural disasters. By 2070, sub-Saharan Africa is expected to be home to more than half of the world’s Christians, while Pakistan is projected to have the largest Muslim population. Pew’s researchers say the projected growth is largely taking place in countries where each faith is already predominant, rather than reflecting a direct shift from one religion to the other.

Canada’s federal government will not appeal an Alberta Court of Appeal ruling that parts of the Impact Assessment Act exceed federal authority and says it will amend the law to address the ruling. They are expected to be developed alongside Bill C-39, now before Parliament, which would shorten project reviews and shift assessments of pipelines, power lines and some nuclear and uranium projects to specialist regulators.

Student and teacher groups have called for a strike on Tuesday, while France’s Senate is scheduled to begin debating the government’s 2027 budget proposal on Nov. 20.

At least 16 people have died and about 600 have been hospitalized after drinking suspected adulterated liquor in Manipur’s Chandel district, state officials said. The precise cause of the deaths and whether the liquor contained methanol remain unconfirmed pending medical findings and laboratory tests. items.title: [cyberscoop.com] Europol-led operation seizes malware infrastructure, finds 6.4 million stolen credentials
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Law enforcement agencies in nine countries, coordinated by Europol and Eurojust, disrupted infrastructure used by Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC, seizing 235 servers and 257 domains and identifying 6.4 million stolen credential records. German authorities said the records came from more than 40,000 victims. The malware services enabled credential theft, remote access and the delivery of ransomware; investigators also cleaned 681 websites compromised to spread Gootloader. Authorities plan to share victim data with notification services, including Have I Been Pwned. On Nov. 13, that service listed 179,745 email addresses linked to CastleRAT infections and 893,000 unique passwords observed more than 3 million times on infected computers. Police advised WordPress users to change credentials, enable multifactor authentication and patch vulnerabilities.

items.title: [arstechnica.com] FAA plans to replace floppy-based air traffic systems by 2028
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

The Federal Aviation Administration plans to replace four aging information systems that rely on floppy disks with a unified digital platform at 435 air traffic facilities by the end of 2028. The new Enterprise Information Display System, or E-IDS, will consolidate weather alerts, airport status and flight notices that controllers currently retrieve through outdated, often manual processes. The FAA says the platform will give controllers faster access to safety-critical information and reduce maintenance problems. The agency has already upgraded five sites, while Congress has provided $12.5 billion for broader air traffic control modernization. The FAA is seeking additional funding through the proposed Modern Skies Act. The agency plans to deploy the system at the remaining locations by the end of 2028.

The new Enterprise Information Display System, or E-IDS, will consolidate weather alerts, airport status and flight notices that controllers currently retrieve through outdated, often manual processes (arstechnica.com, techspot.com, theregister.com). The FAA says the platform will give controllers faster access to safety-critical information and reduce maintenance problems. The agency has already upgraded five sites, while Congress has provided $12.5 billion for broader air traffic control modernization. The FAA is seeking additional funding through the proposed Modern Skies Act (pcmag.com, theregister.com). The agency plans to deploy the system at the remaining locations by the end of 2028 (arstechnica.com). First locations: The five upgraded sites are Atlantic City, Nashville and Greater Rochester international airports, plus FAA data-processing hubs in Atlanta and Salt Lake City (techspot.com, pcmag.com). Systems replaced: E-IDS will replace IDS-4, ACE-IDS, NIDS and ERIDS, which separately provide weather, airport, airspace and en-route flight information (arstechnica.com, theregister.com). Safety record: A 2023 NOTAM system failure following the accidental deletion of a file temporarily halted domestic flight departures nationwide (theregister.com). Funding gap: The FAA says the proposed Modern Skies Act would provide $30 billion for modernization. A September Government Accountability Office report said the overhaul’s second phase needed a further $10.2 billion and had no completion date (theregister.com).

Timeline: August 2020: The FAA awarded Leidos the E-IDS design and development contract (arstechnica.com)
Timeline: 2023: The deletion of a NOTAM file temporarily halted domestic flight departures nationwide (theregister.com)
Timeline: 5 November 2026: The FAA announced the modernization plan and initial E-IDS rollout (mashdigi.com)
Background: E-IDS is part of the FAA’s Next Generation Air Transportation System modernization effort, which dates to 2008 (arstechnica.com).
